title: Taiwan to Basel
subtitle: Electronic components for a Swiss machine maker, checked leg by leg
note: The machine maker is an example. The supplier, Delta Electronics, is named only to show the supplier check; nothing is alleged. Every finding is an Antevo engine's answer on the date shown. Antevo's research desks did not answer on 25 November, so the parts they cover are marked not checked rather than filled in.

tries.label: Leg by leg
tries.source: Antevo Guard, Antevo Executive Brief and Antevo Strategy Radar, 25 Nov 2026 · domain registries, public DNS, USGS, GDACS and EONET disaster alerts, UCDP conflict data

items.name: The supplier
evidence: deltaww.com was registered on 14 February 2001 and points to a web server, not a parking page
Taiwan's company register is not covered by Guard yet, so whether the company is on it was not checked

items.name: Leaving Taiwan and China
evidence: China has paused its curbs on critical-material exports until January

Washington is reported to be readying higher tariffs on China and more than a dozen other economies; the risk Antevo names is Beijing restoring the curbs in reply (high impact, medium probability, rising)

items.name: The sea route
evidence: Bab el-Mandeb, the southern gate of the Red Sea, borders Yemen, Djibouti and Eritrea; Yemen ranks third and Somalia fourth on Antevo's hotspot list (fatalities counted 23 to 30 September)
No storm or earthquake alerts at the Taiwanese or southern Chinese ports, in the Malacca Strait or at Suez from 18 to 25 November

items.name: Rotterdam and the Rhine to Basel
evidence: Antevo's shipping desk, which reads ports and inland waterways, did not answer on 25 November
The Rhine gauges and the Swiss Rhine ports publish their own figures: links below

items.name: Fuel and freight
evidence: Brent rebounded to 91.40 dollars on 24 November; diesel and jet fuel are tight even though gasoline is plentiful
Container freight rates were not checked: the shipping desk did not answer

steps.label: Before the next order, with the links

items.do: Check the supplier on Taiwan's company register
items.why: Guard does not cover Taiwan yet; the Ministry of Economic Affairs keeps the register.

items.do: Settle who pays a new tariff or a restored export curb
items.why: Strategy Radar's options: a price clause on orders for spring delivery, or a second supplier outside the named economies.

items.do: Decide how much stock of parts made with critical materials to hold into January
items.why: China's pause runs to January; extra stock buys time if the curbs return, as long as it can be stored.

items.do: Ask your forwarder whether the ships go by Suez or the Cape, and check the Rhine before booking the barge
items.why: The route sets the transit time, and the river levels and port notices are public.

items.do: Check the duty and the origin rules for each part
items.why: The Swiss customs tariff gives both for each product code.
Strategy Radar is read daily and free; the entries above change as the news does.

sections.title: Tariffs and export curbs
sections.so_what: For a buyer of magnets the risk is the reply: ask suppliers now how they would price parts if the curbs return in January.
evidence: Tariff plans are reported for this week; rates and dates are not yet published
China's pause on its mineral export curbs runs out in January, the month the levies would bite
sections.source: Antevo Strategy Radar and Antevo Executive Brief, 25 Nov 2026

sections.title: Strikes in the region
sections.so_what: Ask the forwarder to price both routes, so a switch to the Cape is a known cost and time, not a surprise.
evidence: Attacks on vessels near Hormuz persist and Houthi drones hit Riyadh on 24 November: severe impact, medium likelihood, rising
Strategy Radar's trigger: act if attacks on merchant ships increase or insurers withdraw cover for Gulf transits

sections.title: Fuel
sections.so_what: Check how the fuel surcharge in your freight contract follows the oil price: the clause decides who carries a jump.
evidence: Brent at 91.40 dollars on 24 November, after talks hoped for with Iran produced nothing
Watch 95 dollars on the upside and 88 on the downside, and the price of diesel

sections.title: Chinese factories
sections.so_what: A reading still below 50 is a reason to ask suppliers about lead times early.
evidence: China's official manufacturing survey for November, consensus 49.7 after 49.3
Below 50 with tariffs pending would show factories bracing for a second trade shock

links.text: The tariff plans and China's pause come to a head in the same month, so for a buyer of magnets the tariff risk and the export-curb risk are one risk with one date: January.
No storm or earthquake alerts on the route this week, but strikes in the region are rising: what could change the timing is the route, not the weather.

watch: China's official manufacturing survey on 30 November (consensus 49.7)
Publication of the US tariff rates and dates, and Beijing's answer
China's critical-material export rules in January
Brent against 95 dollars up and 88 down, and war-risk cover for Gulf transits
disclaimer: From Antevo answers and public records, each dated. A quiet week means no alerts in the sources read, not a safe route. The options are for you to decide on; not advice.
